key_patterns.name: Heterogeneous risk perception
key_patterns.description: risk_perception is continuous on [0,1] and typically right-skewed; varies by age_group and occupation.
key_patterns.relevance: Supports heterogeneous thresholds or propensities for mask adoption; informs individual-level parameters and subgroup targeting.

key_patterns.name: Multiplex homophily
key_patterns.description: Edges in family and work_school layers strongly assort by age_group and occupation; community layer is more mixed but still shows homophily.
key_patterns.relevance: Homophily increases local reinforcement; calibrate layer-specific influence weights and subgroup mixing matrices.

key_patterns.name: Layer density and clustering gradient
key_patterns.description: family layer: low degree, high clustering; work_school: moderate degree, moderate clustering; community: broader degree spread, lower clustering with heavy-tail degree.
key_patterns.relevance: Layer-specific contact frequencies and influence strengths should differ; cascades will originate/stabilize differently across layers.

key_patterns.name: Temporal staging: information precedes adoption
key_patterns.description: received_info transitions generally occur before wearing_mask transitions with a short lag for many agents.
key_patterns.relevance: Model information diffusion and adoption as coupled but distinct processes; include info-to-adoption delay.

key_patterns.name: S-shaped adoption trajectory
key_patterns.description: Aggregate wearing_mask adoption rate over time exhibits a sigmoid (slow start, rapid rise, saturation).
key_patterns.relevance: Suggests threshold or logistic social influence; use to validate macro fit and tune peer influence parameters.

key_patterns.name: Peer effect thresholding
key_patterns.description: Adoption hazard increases nonlinearly with neighbors’ adoption fraction (especially within family and work/school).
key_patterns.relevance: Supports a threshold or logistic response to local adoption; motivates layer-weighted peer influence.

key_patterns.name: Subgroup inequality in adoption
key_patterns.description: Adoption rates differ by age_group and occupation; older and healthcare/white-collar occupations often adopt earlier/higher.
key_patterns.relevance: Track adoption_inequality; calibrate subgroup-specific parameters (baseline propensity, peer sensitivity).

key_patterns.name: Edge directionality inconsistencies
key_patterns.description: social_network.json may have asymmetric ties; undirected influence requires symmetrization or explicit direction handling.
key_patterns.relevance: Influence flow depends on edge direction; choose policy consistently to avoid bias in peer exposure estimates.

key_distributions.name: Risk perception distribution
key_distributions.description: risk_perception ∈ [0,1]; well-modeled by a Beta distribution, potentially stratified by age_group/occupation.
key_distributions.parameters: Beta(α, β) per subgroup; estimate via MLE or method-of-moments

key_distributions.name: Degree distributions by layer
key_distributions.description: family: narrow (often 2–6); work_school: moderate with workplace/school variation; community: overdispersed with heavy tail.
key_distributions.parameters: family ~ Poisson(λ_f) or narrow NB; work_school ~ NB(k_ws, p_ws); community ~ NB(k_c, p_c) or truncated power-law

key_distributions.name: Info arrival waiting time
key_distributions.description: Time from day 0 to first received_info=true event per agent; often geometric/exponential-like.
key_distributions.parameters: Geometric(p_info) or Exponential(λ_info) hazard; stratify by layer exposure

key_distributions.name: Adoption delay after info
key_distributions.description: Time lag between first received_info=true and first wearing_mask=true.
key_distributions.parameters: Shifted geometric with shift δ (minimum lag) and success prob p_adopt|info

key_distributions.name: Initial adoption and info prevalence
key_distributions.description: At day 0, a fraction of agents already wear masks and/or have info.
key_distributions.parameters: p0_mask, p0_info overall and by subgroup

key_relationships.relationship: Higher risk_perception associates with higher initial mask probability.
key_relationships.strength: Quantify via logistic regression OR; expected positive (OR > 1), estimate from day 0 snapshot.

key_relationships.relationship: Conditional on info, higher risk_perception increases adoption hazard.
key_relationships.strength: Positive coefficient in discrete-time hazard model; magnitude to estimate.

key_relationships.relationship: Adoption hazard increases with the fraction of neighbors wearing masks; stronger within family and work_school layers.
key_relationships.strength: Layer-weighted coefficients; typically family > work_school > community.

key_relationships.relationship: Receiving information substantially increases the probability of adopting in subsequent days.
key_relationships.strength: Large positive effect; estimate as odds ratio or hazard ratio.

key_relationships.relationship: Students and white-collar roles have higher work_school degrees; community degree varies by occupation.
key_relationships.strength: Moderate to strong; use ANOVA or regression on degree.

key_relationships.relationship: Asymmetry in edges can bias neighbor exposure; symmetrization changes measured peer effects.
key_relationships.strength: Methodological; assess with sensitivity analysis (directed vs. undirected).

risk_threshold_mapping.notes: Maps intrinsic risk to social threshold; can be blended with logistic adoption.

initial_mask_probability.value: logit(p0_i) = α0 + α_age[age_group_i] + α_occ[occupation_i] + α_r * risk_perception_i
initial_mask_probability.notes: Estimate coefficients via logistic regression on day 0 wearing_mask.

abandonment_probability_per_day.value: estimate from false→true→false transitions; default 0 if monotonic adoption observed
abandonment_probability_per_day.notes: If mask-wearing is sticky, set near zero; otherwise include habit decay.

symmetrize_edges.notes: Alternatively, preserve direction and compute in- vs out-neighborhoods; calibrate sensitivity.

layer_influence_weights.source: Calibrated using hazard model with neighbor adoption by layer
layer_influence_weights.notes: Initialize with prior ordering family > work_school > community; refine via calibration to RMSE/MAE.

edge_activation_rate_per_day.source: Literature priors and adjusted by matching info/adoption hazards
edge_activation_rate_per_day.notes: Probability an edge is active per day; affects exposure counts.

degree_capping_or_weighting.value: cap community degree at 99th percentile or weight exposures by 1/deg to avoid superspreader bias

adoption_rule.value: logistic-threshold hybrid: P(adopt_i,t) = σ(β0 + β_info * I_i,t + Σ_L β_L * f_L,i,t − γ * threshold_i)
adoption_rule.source: day-agent time series (hazard model), agent CSV, social_network.json
adoption_rule.notes: f_L,i,t = neighbor mask fraction in layer L at time t; I_i,t indicates received_info.

peer_influence_coefficients.source: day-agent time series with neighbor exposure features by layer
peer_influence_coefficients.notes: Estimate via discrete-time survival/logistic regression with clustered SEs.

information_effect_coefficient.notes: Captures jump in adoption hazard after info.

social_noise_sigma.source: Calibration to match adoption_rate_over_time variance across runs
social_noise_sigma.notes: Randomness in decision beyond observed covariates.

broadcast_rate_per_day.value: to_estimate from info hazards not explained by peer contacts

peer_info_transmission_probability.source: day-agent time series + social_network.json (info exposure along edges)
peer_info_transmission_probability.notes: Probability info passes along an active edge per day.

info_to_adoption_min_lag_days.source: day-agent time series (time between first info and adoption)
info_to_adoption_min_lag_days.notes: Implement as a refractory period before adoption is allowed.

seed_strategy.value: probabilistic seeding using p0_i; optional boost for high-risk_perception or high-degree nodes
seed_strategy.notes: Aligns simulation initial state with observed day 0.

initial_info_state.value: set received_info_i,0 from data; if missing, draw from p0_info by subgroup
initial_info_state.notes: Ensures consistency with observed information baseline.

mandate_day.source: external policy timeline or inferred change-point in adoption
mandate_day.notes: If a mandate exists, include as exogenous shock.

mandate_effect_multiplier.value: multiply β_info or add policy term β_policy at/after mandate_day
mandate_effect_multiplier.source: calibration via change-point regression on adoption hazard
mandate_effect_multiplier.notes: Captures shifts due to policy or media events.

subgroup_targets.value: adoption rates by age_group and occupation

preprocessing_steps.purpose: Ensure agent_id uniqueness in agent CSV; all IDs in social_network.json exist; no self-loops; deduplicate edges.

preprocessing_steps.step: Symmetrize or direct edges by policy
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Create consistent adjacency per layer; store both directed and undirected for sensitivity analysis.
For each agent-day, compute fraction of neighbors wearing masks by layer; also compute info-exposed neighbors.
Identify first day of received_info and wearing_mask adoption per agent; compute lags and hazards.
Fit Beta(α,β) for risk_perception (overall and by subgroup); summarize degree distributions per layer.
Temporal split (e.g., first 70% days train, last 30% validate); also stratify by subgroups to check generalization.
Compute observed adoption_rate_over_time and subgroup series for calibration objectives.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Two-stage micro-to-macro. Stage 1: Fit discrete-time hazard models. (a) Information diffusion: P(received_info_t+1=1 | state_t) = σ(θ0 + Σ_L θ_L * info_neighbor_fraction_L + θ_bcast). (b) Adoption given info: P(adopt_t+1=1 | state_t, received_info=1) = σ(β0 + β_info + Σ_L β_L * neighbor_mask_fraction_L + β_r * risk_perception + β_age + β_occ). Extract coefficients and lags; translate to simulation parameters (layer weights, broadcast rate, info effect, peer influence, threshold mapping). Stage 2: Macro calibration via simulation. Initialize agents to match day 0 states; run many replicates; use Bayesian optimization or approximate Bayesian computation to minimize RMSE_to_observed and MAE_to_observed over a parameter subset (peer weights, edge activation rates, noise, abandonment, mandate effects). Include subgroup targets and adoption_inequality as secondary objectives/constraints. Conduct sensitivity analysis on edge symmetrization and degree capping.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Hold out last 30% of days for validation; compute RMSE_to_observed, MAE_to_observed, and R_squared on aggregate and by subgroup. Validate peak_adoption and time_to_threshold (40%, 60%, 80%) with confidence intervals from replicate runs. Perform posterior predictive checks on distribution of adoption delays and info lags. Cross-validate across network layers by simulating with perturbed layer weights to test robustness. Report calibration uncertainty via parameter posterior samples or bootstrap.

file_summaries:
- Data structure and type: Flat CSV table; one row per agent. No nested structures. agent_id is the unique primary key. Suitable to load as a node-attribute table for a graph-based simulation.
- Columns and meanings:
  - agent_id (int): Unique identifier to join with network edges and reference in the simulation.
  - age_group (categorical string): Demographic cohort (e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age). Use for homophily, contact mixing matrices, and possibly age-specific norms/compliance.
  - occupation (categorical string): Social role/context (e.g., Student, Blue Collar, White Collar). Use to assign agents to interaction layers (school, workplace) and contact rates.
  - risk_perception (float in [0,1]): Baseline perception of disease/behavioral risk; higher values imply stronger intrinsic tendency to wear masks or lower threshold for adoption.
- Relationships or nested elements: None within the file. Relationships arise externally by:
  - Joining to a social network (edges) via agent_id.
  - Grouping agents into layers (household, school, workplace, community) based on age_group and occupation.
- How this informs simulation entities/interactions:
  - Initialize agent attributes: age_group, occupation, risk_perception attach directly to each agent node.
  - Behavior seeding: Use risk_perception as initial mask-wearing probability or as part of a logistic propensity score.
  - Influence dynamics: Set adoption thresholds inversely related to risk_perception (e.g., threshold ≈ 1 − risk_perception) or modulate susceptibility to peer influence.
  - Network formation/mixing: Use age_group and occupation to drive homophily and to place agents in specific contact layers with different interaction frequencies.
  - Heterogeneity: Allow age/occupation-specific parameters (peer influence weight, conformity pressure, visibility of behavior) and different exogenous policy effects.
  - Data quality: Expect categorical encoding for age_group/occupation; verify uniqueness of agent_id and that risk_perception is bounded [0,1].

Semantic metadata summary for social_network.json

- Data structure and type:
  - JSON object representing a multiplex (layered) social network.
  - Top-level is a dictionary/map: key = agent ID (as string), value = an object with arrays of neighbor IDs per social context.

- Meaning of keys/columns:
  - Top-level keys like "0", "1", "2": unique person/agent identifiers (convertible to integers).
  - Nested keys:
    - family: list of agent IDs connected via family ties.
    - work_school: list of agent IDs connected via work or school ties.
    - community: list of agent IDs connected via broader community ties (neighbors, friends, casual social).

- Relationships and nested elements:
  - Each agent maps to three adjacency lists (one per layer). Lists contain integer IDs that reference other agents in the same global ID space.
  - Edges are unweighted and may be asymmetric in the file (i.e., presence of A→B does not guarantee B→A); decide whether to symmetrize for undirected influence or preserve directionality.
  - Layers are disjoint categories; a neighbor may appear in multiple layers (possible multiplex overlap).
  - Missing or empty lists (if present in full data) should be treated as no ties in that layer.
  - No self-loops are expected; none shown.
  - No node attributes (e.g., initial mask status) or edge weights/frequencies are included.

- How this data should inform simulation entities/interactions:
  - Agents: instantiate one agent per top-level key; store ID and layer-specific neighbor sets.
  - Network layers: build three separate graphs (family, work_school, community) or a single multiplex structure; optionally assign layer-specific interaction frequencies and influence strengths (e.g., family > work/school > community).
  - Interaction scheduling: sample contacts within layers according to chosen rates; multiplex overlap can increase effective exposure.
  - Influence dynamics: propagate mask-wearing behavior along edges; handle directed or undirected influence per design; apply layer-dependent adoption probabilities or weights.
  - Initialization: since the file lacks behavioral states, generate initial mask-wearing seeds and any agent attributes exogenously.
  - Validation: ensure all referenced neighbor IDs exist as agents; decide on deduplication within lists and symmetrization policy before building adjacency structures.

- Data structure and type
  - CSV file; flat, long-format time series.
  - One record per (day, agent_id) pair. Primary key: (day, agent_id).
  - Columns: day:int, agent_id:int, wearing_mask:bool, received_info:bool.

- Meaning of keys/columns
  - day: Discrete simulation timestep (e.g., 0, 1, 2, …).
  - agent_id: Unique identifier for an individual agent, repeated across days.
  - wearing_mask: Agent’s behavioral state at that day (adopted mask-wearing or not).
  - received_info: Whether the agent has received information about mask-wearing (via broadcast or social contact) by that day.

- Relationships or nested elements
  - No nesting; purely tabular.
  - Temporal linkage: rows with the same agent_id across increasing day values form each agent’s trajectory.
  - State transitions can be inferred by comparing consecutive days per agent (e.g., false→true for wearing_mask indicates adoption event; similarly for received_info).
  - Network structure is not present; any social ties must come from another source or be generated.

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
  - Initialize agents: At day 0, set wearing_mask and received_info from the file.
  - Define state variables per agent: mask_state, info_state.
  - Calibrate transition rules: Estimate probabilities/hazards of adopting a mask given info_state and (if available) neighbor adoption; disentangle baseline adoption (without info) vs. info-triggered adoption.
  - Model information diffusion: received_info changes indicate exposure events; use them to fit or validate info spread parameters (broadcast rate, peer-to-peer transmission).
  - Validation: Compare simulated trajectories of wearing_mask and received_info against observed sequences across days.
  - If network data is absent, assume or generate a network topology; use this file to fit non-network parameters and initial conditions.
